theme.title: Rock bottom
theme.subtitle: The NBA's worst seasons
theme.recap: The 1972–73 Sixers and 2011–12 Bobcats own the worst records ever, and both lost games in long runs.

questions.prompt: How many games did the 1972–73 Philadelphia 76ers win?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the 76ers lost their remaining 13 games to finish 9–73.

funFacts.text: Philadelphia lost its first 15 games before the season unraveled further.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the 76ers lost their first 15 games of the season

funFacts.text: Veteran Hal Greer was the last holdover from the 1967 championship team and retired after the season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Only Hal Greer remained on the roster from the 1966–1967 NBA Championship Team

funFacts.text: The Sixers had offered the coaching job to both Al McGuire and Adolph Rupp, but each declined.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Sixers ownership offered the head coaching job to Marquette University head coach Al McGuire

questions.prompt: In the lockout-shortened 2011–12 season, how many games did the Charlotte Bobcats win?
questions.note: Seven, the lowest winning percentage in NBA history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Total: 7–59 (Home: 4–29; Road: 3–30)

funFacts.text: Michael Jordan owned Charlotte during its historically difficult season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Owner  | Michael Jordan

funFacts.text: Gerald Henderson led the Bobcats in scoring with 15.1 points per game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Gerald Henderson led the team in scoring, with an average of 15.1 points per game

funFacts.text: Kemba Walker joined the team as a rookie after Charlotte selected him in the first round of the draft.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 1 | 9 | Kemba Walker

questions.prompt: How many games behind first-place Boston did the 1972–73 Sixers finish in their division?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 76ers finished an NBA-record 59 games behind the Atlantic Division champion Boston Celtics.

funFacts.text: Only six seasons earlier, Philadelphia had set an NBA record for regular-season wins.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Only six seasons earlier, the 76ers had set the NBA record for most wins in a season

funFacts.text: Philadelphia's average scoring margin was an abysmal minus 12.1 points per game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: their −12.1 points per game point differential

funFacts.text: The struggling roster was playing its tenth season in Philadelphia.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: their 24th season in the NBA and tenth in Philadelphia

questions.prompt: The 2011–12 Bobcats closed the season on a losing streak that wasn’t snapped until the next season began. How long was it?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: embarking on a 23-game losing streak that lasted until the start of the following season.

funFacts.text: Charlotte's last victory before the drought came against Toronto in mid-March.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: On March 17, 2012, the Bobcats had their final win of the season against the Toronto Raptors

funFacts.text: The season ended with a 104–84 defeat against the New York Knicks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: losing 104–84 to the New York Knicks in their final regular season game

funFacts.text: Bismack Biyombo led Charlotte in rebounds, while D. J. Augustin led in assists.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bismack Biyombo led in rebounds per game (5.8), and point guard D. J. Augustin

questions.prompt: The 2013–14 Sixers tied what was then the NBA record for consecutive losses. How many?
questions.note: 26 in a row, matching Cleveland's mark.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: tying Cleveland's former NBA record for most consecutive losses with 26

funFacts.text: The Sixers finally ended the run with a 123–98 win against Detroit at home.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: ended with a 123–98 win over the Detroit Pistons on March 29

funFacts.text: Rookie guard Michael Carter-Williams won Rookie of the Year that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Michael Carter-Williams enjoyed a successful rookie season, earning Rookie of the Year honors

funFacts.text: Sam Hinkie was Philadelphia's general manager during the difficult season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: General manager  | Sam Hinkie
